title: Getting Started with Odiffr
text: Generate standalone HTML reports QA review: Reports include: - Pass/fail statistics visual cards - Failure reason breakdown - Diff statistics (min, median, mean, max) - Worst offenders table thumbnails (diff image default; baseline, current diff side side images = ""; click thumbnail see full-size image) relative_paths option useful want move share report along diff images folder. relative paths, report find images regardless files moved.

title: Getting Started with Odiffr
text: Two functions write batch results formats CI systems understand: batch_markdown() produces GitHub-flavoured Markdown summary (pass/fail line, failure reasons worst offenders table). GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY environment variable set, GitHub Actions, summary appended file shows job’s summary page. Elsewhere returns Markdown string. batch_junit() writes JUnit XML report one test case per comparison. Differences missing files failures, comparisons run errors. CI test reporters can display . complete GitHub Actions step:
code: results <- compare_image_dirs("baseline/", "current/", diff_dir = "diffs/")  batch_markdown(results)                    # GitHub job summary batch_junit(results, "odiffr-junit.xml")   # JUnit XML batch_report(results, "diffs/report.html", images = "all", embed = TRUE) - name: Compare images   run: |     library(odiffr)     results <- compare_image_dirs("baseline/", "current/", diff_dir = "diffs/")     batch_markdown(results)     batch_junit(results, "odiffr-junit.xml")     batch_report(results, "diffs/report.html", images = "all",                  embed = TRUE)     if (any(!results$match)) stop("Visual regression detected!")   shell: Rscript {0}  - name: Upload diffs and report   if: always()   uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4   with:     name: visual-diffs     path: |       diffs/       odiffr-junit.xml

title: Getting Started with Odiffr
text: audit_record() turns comparison results documented, machine-readable evidence record supports audit trails. every comparison records image paths hashes sizes, diff image () hash, outcome (match, reason, diff_count, diff_percentage, error). header records schema version ("odiffr-audit/1"), UTC timestamp, odiffr odiff versions, odiff binary path hash, R version, platform user, comparison parameters. SHA-256 hashing uses openssl digest package; use hash = "md5" rely base R . Files hashed audit_record() called, create record straight comparison. See ?audit_record full schema.
code: # odiff_run() results carry their parameters result <- odiff_run("baseline.png", "current.png", "diff.png",                     threshold = 0.05) rec <- audit_record(result) rec$header$odiff_version rec$comparisons[, c("img1_hash", "img2_hash", "match")]  # Write a JSON evidence file (requires jsonlite) audit_record(result, file = "validation/comparison-audit.json")  # Batch results: pass the parameters you used; CSV has one row per pair results <- compare_image_dirs("baseline/", "current/", threshold = 0.05) audit_record(results, file = "validation/audit.csv", format = "csv",              params = list(threshold = 0.05))

Comparing underlying data catches many problems, : changed font, shifted legend, different default theme package upgrade, truncated table show rendered output. compare_pdfs() renders page two PDF files image compares page page odiff. get result per page, odiff’s tolerance (threshold) antialiasing handling, optional diff images highlighting changed pixels, summaries reports image comparisons. Typical uses: Production versus QC outputs: compare figure produced production program one produced independent QC program. Re-running outputs upgrade: re-run outputs upgrading R packages compare outputs upgrade. Rendered documents: compare Quarto R Markdown document rendered PDF change. title: Using odiffr with shinytest2
text: shinytest2 can take screenshots running Shiny app app$expect_screenshot() store testthat snapshots. documentation calls screenshots brittle kind expectation, good reasons: default screenshot must match stored snapshot exactly (within blur-based threshold). Chromium renders edges rounded corners, circles, borders text slightly different anti-aliasing run run machine machine, screenshots look identical often match. screenshot change, get new .new.png file picture changed. odiffr’s compare_file_odiff() plugs compare argument expect_screenshot() addresses : compares images odiff, perceptual colour threshold optional detection anti-aliased pixels. comparison fails, writes diff image highlighting changed pixels prints . odiffr drive browser; shinytest2 still takes screenshots. need odiff binary (see vignette("getting-started")).

title: Using odiffr with shinytest2
text: preset chooses comparison settings (see ?odiff_preset): "screenshot" ignores anti-aliased pixels keeps colour threshold low, real colour change still caught. odiffr’s calibration tests, rounded shapes 1px borders shifted quarter half pixel fail default settings pass "screenshot", new 10 x 10 pixel element 10 x 10 pixel patch changing blue green fails. "cross_platform" also tolerates edges moved half pixel small colour gamma shifts. price can miss changes colours similar brightness (blue green) faint elements. Arguments pass explicitly override preset, can still add ignore_regions, e.g. clock random plot:
code: app$expect_screenshot(   compare = odiffr::compare_file_odiff(     preset = "screenshot",     threshold = 0.15,     ignore_regions = list(odiffr::ignore_region(0, 0, 300, 40))   ) )
